title: spec review: S1 v5: executor_identity resolves any executor field to provider/model; review rule compares models with None guard
spec:
Respec of T-1344 after spec review T-1345. Goal T-1334: [[executors]] provider-agnostic; S2 (depends on this) wires dispatch. S1 and S2 reach main together in one goal PR; the Planner adds the first provider="claude" row to pool.toml only after both merge. Rollback: git revert (no persisted state, no pool.toml field).

1. orchestrator/pool.py: factor the row source out of Pool._read_executors (pool.py:157) into executor_rows(cfg) -> list[dict]: cfg["executors"] (a list of dicts keyed by "id") or, when absent/empty, the synthesized LEGACY_EXECUTOR_ID row exactly as today; Pool._read_executors uses it (duplicate ids: last wins, as today). Module function executor_identity(field, cfg) -> {"provider": "codex"|"claude"|None, "model": str|None}: row whose "id" == field in executor_rows(cfg) -> its provider/model; "claude:<tier>" (legacy, spawn.py:1564) -> "claude", model cfg.get("models",{}).get(tier) only if tier in ("haiku","sonnet","opus") and a str, else None; None/unknown -> both None. No Pool state, no disk. Pool.executor_identity(field), Pool.is_claude_executor(field) delegate with self.cfg.
2. pool.py eligible_executors (pool.py:522): claude rows pass every existing check (enabled, roles, cooling, band, roll_day, max_parallel, daily_budget_tasks) and also need headroom on any execute-affinity account: self.pick("execute") at most once per call, lazily, only when a claude row reaches that check; never for codex-only configs (so pick_executor and codex_available never call pick either). Eligibility reserves nothing; S2's dispatch re-picks the account and holds when none is left. codex_available (pool.py:590): True iff some eligible row has provider "codex" (with codex-only rows identical to today: pick_executor returns an eligible row whenever one exists).
3. orchestrator/daemon.py: extend line 13 to `from .pool import Pool, fallback_tier, executor_identity, config as pool_config`; add `import tomllib`.
4. daemon.review_tier(t, cfg=None) (daemon.py:1070), _security_review_tier(t, cfg=None) (daemon.py:1136): legacy branches first, unchanged: review_tier startswith("claude:sonnet") -> "opus", startswith("claude:opus") -> "sonnet"; _security_review_tier exact f"claude:{tier}" -> _other_tier(tier). executor field None -> default, no config read. Otherwise one try: cfg = pool_config() if cfg is None; ident = executor_identity(field, cfg); swap to _other_tier(default) only if ident["provider"] == "claude" and ident["model"] is a str equal to cfg["models"].get(default); else default. except (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError, ValueError, OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as exc: print(f"review_tier: lookup failed ({exc}); failing closed to {other}", file=sys.stderr); return other (other = _other_tier(default)).
5. daemon._open_reviews(t, n_reviews, review_reason, cfg=None) (daemon.py:1212; tier selection daemon.py:1228-1244): when cfg is None, load pool_config() once at the top inside the same try/except (failure -> cfg stays None and each tier call fails closed); pass cfg to every review_tier/_security_review_tier call. daemon.py:1241 becomes: legacy startswith("claude:") or (cfg is not None and executor_identity(t.get("executor"), cfg)["provider"] == "claude"); second review for a Claude executor stays on review_tier(t, cfg). Callers: gate(pool) daemon.py:1432 and sweep_leases(pool) daemon.py:1625 pass cfg=pool.cfg; _merge_reviewed_one daemon.py:1524 passes nothing.

Decided, not in S1 (do not add): running_claude_workers (daemon.py:470), spawn.py:1508, executed_by (daemon.py:392), docstring daemon.py:1348, capacity.py:54, executor.py:279/:487 are S2 or unchanged (row-routed runs still claim "claude:<acct>"). Model-id aliasing (dated vs undated ids) is out of scope: distinct strings are distinct models. No guard test against enabling a claude row early (the goal PR ships S1+S2 together). No pool.toml byte test.
Tests: one method per scenario as named in acceptance; baselines are hard-coded expected values; cfg dicts and accounts (with "execute" affinity) built in-test; patched globals restored. No new dependencies.
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py::ExecutorIdentity::test_identity_row_legacy_unknown: claude row id, codex row id, 'claude:opus', 'claude:success_floor', unknown id and None resolve as specified; with no [[executors]] table the synthesized legacy row resolves to provider codex

tests/test_pool.py::ExecutorIdentity::test_claude_row_needs_account_headroom: claude row excluded when every execute-affinity account is cooling, included with headroom, excluded at max_parallel; pick called at most once per eligible_executors call

tests/test_pool.py::ExecutorIdentity::test_codex_only_never_calls_pick: codex-only cfg -> eligible_executors, pick_executor and codex_available make zero Pool.pick calls and return hard-coded expected values with and without task
tests/test_daemon.py::ReviewModelRule::test_lookup_failure_fails_closed (executor_identity raising KeyError and pool_config raising OSError -> other tier plus the stderr line)
tests/test_daemon.py::ReviewModelRule::test_open_reviews_loads_config_at_most_once (cfg=None -> pool_config called <= 1 time; cfg passed -> 0 times; codex-only tiers match hard-coded values)

risks.issue: Executor.running is counted from bus tasks whose executor equals the row id (pool.py:~168). The spec says row-routed runs still claim 'claude:<acct>', so a claude row's running count stays 0. That makes the max_parallel check a no-op, and the 'excluded at max_parallel' acceptance test only passes if it sets ex.running by hand. Nothing shows the check works end to end before S2 lands.

A claude row with no model, or a model that doesn't match cfg['models'][default], silently keeps the default tier. Executor and reviewer can then be the same model, which is the self-review this rule exists to prevent. The spec fails closed on lookup errors but not on this case. The test name 'modelless_keep_default' pins the silent behaviour.

If pool_config() fails in _open_reviews, cfg stays None. Every codex-executed task then fails closed to 'opus' and prints a stderr line, even though nothing is wrong with the codex path. The number>0 branch (daemon.py:1241) skips the Claude check when cfg is None, and the review then becomes _other_tier(existing[0]['tier']). The two paths can end up inconsistent during a config outage.

_open_reviews loads pool_config() at the top even when t['executor'] is None or a legacy 'claude:' value. That adds a config read per call where review_tier itself makes none, and it is what puts the fail-closed path in reach of unrelated tasks.

codex_available changes meaning: it used to be 'the top-ranked pick is codex' and becomes 'some eligible row is codex'. mcp.py:155, daemon.py:1876 and Pool.status call it. The spec only checks hard-coded values for codex-only and one mixed case. Callers that use it to decide whether Codex can take the task now may get a different answer than pick_executor gives.

executor_identity does not say which row wins when ids are duplicated. _read_executors keeps the last, but a first-match lookup over executor_rows(cfg) would return the first. This is a case where the review tier depends on which row is read.

Acceptance ids carry parenthetical text, for example 'test_claude_row_on_sonnet_model_reviewed_by_opus (review_tier and _security_review_tier)'. The gate that extracts test ids may not strip it, and the spec conditional says ids must match exactly.

suggested_spec_changes: Make the max_parallel acceptance check state how ex.running is populated in the test (set directly, or via a bus task whose executor equals the row id). Say explicitly that max_parallel is not enforced for real claude runs until S2 counts 'claude:<acct>' runs against the row.

Decide what a claude row with a missing or unmatched model does in review_tier and _security_review_tier. Preferably fail closed to _other_tier(default) with the stderr line, and add that to test_lookup_failure_fails_closed. If keeping the default is intended, state why self-review is acceptable there.
In _open_reviews, load cfg lazily, only when the executor is not None and not legacy 'claude:'. This avoids failing closed for codex tasks and makes the 'at most once' rule simpler to test.
State that executor_identity resolves duplicate ids the same way _read_executors does (last wins), and add a test for it.
Move the parenthetical notes out of the acceptance ids into separate lines so the ids match the method names exactly.
Add a test or a note that Pool.status and mcp.py:155 give the same answers for codex-only configs after the codex_available rewrite.
